caseName: Moore, Commissioner of Patents, v. United States Ex Rel. Newcomb Motor Company
caseNameFull: Edward B. Moore, Commissioner of Patents, in Error v. United States of America Ex Rel. Newcomb Motor Company
syllabus: A writ of error to the Court of Appeals of the District of Columbia dismissed for want df jurisdiction without opinion on the authority of Frasch v. Moore, 211 U. S. 1, and other cases cited.
summary: ERROR TO THE COURT OF APPEALS OF THE DISTRICT OF, COLUMBIA.
attorneys: Mr. Frederick P. Fish and Mr. Melville Church, with whom Mr.'Albert G. -Davis was on the briéf,'for plaintiff in error., Mr. Robert N. Kenyon, with whom Mr. Walter F. Rogers and Mr. Charles H.- Duell were on the brief, for defendant in error.

opinions.text:
Per Curiam.

The writ of error is dismissed for want of •jurisdiction. Frasch v. Moore, 211 U. S. 1; Rousseau v. Browne, 21 App. D. C. 73, 80; Johnson v. Mueser, 212 U. S. 284; Atkins v. Moore, 212 U. S. 285; Gaines v. Knecht, 212 U. S. 561; Same v. Same, 27 App. D. C. 530, 532; Taylor v. Taft, 203 U. S. 461; United States v. Lynch, 137 U. S. 280; Baltimore & Potomac R. R. Co. v. Hopkins, 130 U. S. 210, 226. The application for certiorari is also denied.
